packs.name: shacl-projection-pack
packs.description:
Shared, target-agnostic vocabulary and admission gate for "SHACL-shape-driven projection" --
the pattern first built as a one-off inside packs/dspy-pack (dspy:derivedFromShaclShape,
dspy:isOutputField, gates/020_shacl_signature_admission.rq), extracted here so a NEW
projection target (a Pydantic model, a Rust struct, a TypeScript interface, ...) does not
have to re-derive the SHACL-discovery/validation logic from scratch.

Reuses standard SHACL vocabulary directly (sh:NodeShape / sh:PropertyShape / sh:targetClass /
sh:property / sh:path / sh:datatype) -- this pack does not reinvent it. It adds exactly one
new predicate pair on top: sp:derivedFromShape (generalizes dspy:derivedFromShaclShape past
dspy specifically -- "this projected artifact's fields come from this real sh:NodeShape") and
sp:isPrimaryOutput (generalizes dspy:isOutputField -- "this field is a real, rendered field of
the target artifact, not a fabricated default"). The admitted-datatype enum (xsd:string /
xsd:boolean / xsd:integer|xsd:long / xsd:decimal|xsd:float|xsd:double) is the same 4-python-type
mapping dspy-pack's gate already enforces, reused by literal IRI, not reimplemented.

gates/010_shape_validity.rq is the SAME validation dspy-pack's own
gates/020_shacl_signature_admission.rq implements (every reachable sh:PropertyShape must have
both sh:path and sh:datatype; sh:datatype must be one of the 4 admitted XSD types; sh:path's
local name must be a valid, unique-within-shape Python identifier -- refuse, don't
auto-mangle; every projection must have >=1 real sp:isPrimaryOutput field, never a
fabricated default), rewritten generically over sp:derivedFromShape / ANY sh:NodeShape instead
of being hardcoded to dspy:Signature. dspy-pack's own gate is left untouched (round-5 SHACL
feature, 18 passing e2e tests) -- this pack does not replace it, it is the generalized sibling
a second projection target can reuse without composing dspy-pack at all.

REAL LIMITATION, stated precisely rather than overclaimed: ggen packs cannot declare
pack-to-pack dependencies in pack.toml -- there is no [dependencies] table a pack can use to
require another pack be present. This pack's vocabulary/gate is therefore not "depended on" by
any consumer of a second projection-target pack (e.g. packs/shacl-to-pydantic-pack) in any
enforced sense; it is REUSED two ways, both verified against a real `ggen sync run` in this
pack version: (1) by IRI -- a template's SPARQL can query `sp:derivedFromShape`/
`sp:isPrimaryOutput` triples without this pack being present at all, since RDF predicates are
just IRIs, not gated symbols; (2) by explicit composition -- a consumer's OWN ggen.toml lists
BOTH packs.shacl-projection-pack AND packs.shacl-to-pydantic-pack under [packs], and ggen-engine
runs every composed pack's gates/*.rq against the UNION of the merged graph
(crates/ggen-engine/src/sync.rs, "Pack-shipped SPARQL gates" stage) -- so shacl-projection-pack's
gates/010_shape_validity.rq enforces shape validity for shacl-to-pydantic-pack's fields even
though shacl-to-pydantic-pack ships no admission gate of its own. A consumer that composes
shacl-to-pydantic-pack WITHOUT also composing shacl-projection-pack gets the vocabulary (IRIs
are just strings) but NOT the admission gate -- this is the real, confirmed boundary of pack
composition in this codebase, not a dependency mechanism.

Ships zero individuals (pure law, matching dspy-pack's own convention) -- composing this pack
injects no signature, model, or shape into a consumer's generated output. A consumer supplies
its own sh:NodeShape / sp:derivedFromShape individuals in its own .ttl.

packs.name: dogfood-lifecycle-pack
packs.description: v26.7.13 Operation Dogfood session-lifecycle schema: the RDF vocabulary, SHACL shape, and sample fixtures for capturing a Claude Code session's tool events (Bash / Edit / Write / Read / Task / ...) as PROV-O provenance so that ggen can validate a session log. A PostToolUse hook appends one Turtle node per tool event and a session-end recipe runs `ggen graph validate --files <session.ttl> --shapes <shapes.ttl>`; this pack authors the vocabulary + shape + fixtures that loop targets (the hook and recipe themselves are wired by the parent session, not here). PUBLIC-ONTOLOGY-FIRST (mirrors packs/soc2-audit-pack and packs/dry-run-publish-pack): every relationship reuses a public vocabulary where one fits — prov: (Activity for the session and each tool event, Agent for the operator and subagents, used/generated/wasAssociatedWith/actedOnBehalfOf), dcterms: (identifier for the session id, isPartOf for the tool-event -> session ref, description), skos: (ConceptScheme + notation for the closed tool-name and outcome vocabularies), time: (inXSDDateTimeStamp for the wall-independent event timestamp). Content-addressed tool inputs/outputs use the repo's existing urn:blake3:<hex> scheme (crates/chatman-common provenance::content_address, crates/cng pipeline.rs ImportedArtifact). DISCLOSED MINTED TERMS (capability-justified, no public equivalent — each carries an rdfs:comment in ontology.ttl naming the checked public ontologies and why they do not fit): dfl:Session and dfl:ToolEvent (rdfs:subClassOf prov:Activity — PROV has no subtype distinguishing a session-scoped activity from a single tool invocation, and SHACL needs a precise sh:targetClass to require tool-event properties without imposing them on the session node); dfl:sequenceIndex (monotonic per-session ordinal — PROV has no event ordinal, OLO's olo:index requires full ordered-list slot membership); dfl:outcome + dfl:Outcome (a tool event's terminal status drawn from a CLOSED 3-value vocab ok/error/blocked — mirrors packs/jira-tracking-pack's closed jira:Status scheme; no public ontology enumerates tool-invocation outcomes). OBSERVATION-ONLY FENCE (structural, not merely stated): this pack MODELS the session lifecycle as observation/provenance; it never asserts authority, permission, or actuation — those are separate governed surfaces (admission, hooks, receipts in crates/praxis-graphlaw/src/chatman). No class, predicate, or individual here is named 'authorize', 'permit', 'grant', 'actuate', or 'execute'; the outcome vocabulary records what a tool event OBSERVABLY did (ok/error/blocked), never that it was permitted to. No external ontology is unioned — this pack's vocabulary is self-contained PROV/DCMI/SKOS/OWL-Time, so no ggen.toml extra_ontologies entry is required. No private namespace is minted beyond the disclosed capability-justified terms above.

packs.name: cargo-cicd-pack
packs.description: Typed Rust catalog + reference doc + inject-mode mod-wiring, generated from a source-audited command-surface vocabulary for ~/cargo-cicd (crates.io `cargo-cicd`, real dependency: clap-noun-verb 26.6.2, confirmed via its Cargo.toml). Round 2 (2026-07-18) replaced the original README-only transcription with a dated source audit against ~/cargo-cicd v26.7.6 (src/nouns/*.rs) -- 52 commands across 21 nouns, each carrying a cc:sourceFile citation; 9 rows additionally carry cc:targetOntologyConcept linking to cargo-cicd's own real SKOS/PROV-O ontology. The generated catalog gained two new real functions (parse_args, args_are_consistent) plus 4 new adversarial/consistency proof tests exercising them against every row, not a hand-picked sample. All three regenerable artifacts (catalog, proof, reference doc) switched from force:true to freeze_policy:checksum/freeze_slots_dir -- live-verified in a scratch consumer: a hand-edit to the generated catalog now makes the next `ggen sync run` report 'skipped: frozen: ... manual edit detected' instead of silently clobbering it, while an unedited file still round-trips as 'skipped: unchanged'. cc:doctor-bare is retained, deprecated, for backward compatibility with the pre-audit bare-noun shape. Round 4 (2026-07-19) added the first real error/return-type facts: re-audited ~/cargo-cicd's 21 nouns/*.rs files (grep-confirmed every #[verb] cmd_* returns clap_noun_verb::Result<()>, uniform across all 51 live rows) and cross-referenced the real dependency ~/clap-noun-verb/src/error.rs for the 10 actual NounVerbError variant names (transcribed verbatim, not paraphrased) -- correction, see Round 6: the enum itself carries no #[non_exhaustive] attribute in that file; only the 10 variant names were verbatim, the attribute claim was not. Generated catalog gained CARGO_CICD_RETURN_TYPE/CARGO_CICD_ERROR_ENUM/CARGO_CICD_ERROR_VARIANTS constants plus all_commands_share_return_contract(); proof gained 4 new tests (15 total, up from 11) covering exact-count drift, sortedness/dedup, and contract uniformity. Live-verified end-to-end in a scratch consumer (ggen sync run, real cargo test): 15/15 passing. This closes part of Ontology expressiveness/Target-API fidelity's L3 'error cases' gap that Round 3 explicitly left open, but stops short of L3 in full: no per-command error-path (which variant a given command actually raises) or exit-code facts are modeled -- only the shared enum-level contract, uniform across all rows. Round 5 (2026-07-21, L5 wave 5) closed the handler-gap dimension named in .specify/maturity.ttl's cg_010 mat:d2 ('L1 -- nothing callable, catalog only, no cargo-cicd invocation'): first checked directly (per the task's own instruction) whether this pack's existing generated proof (tests/cargo_cicd_catalog_proof.rs, the 15/15-passing artifact mat:d5 cites) hand-transcribes expected values the way praxis-core-pack/star-toml-pack's ORIGINAL proofs did -- it does not; both its `rows`/`error_variants` sparql: queries are byte-identical to the ones cargo_cicd_catalog.rs.tmpl already uses, rendered via a from-scratch Tera for-loop, so the cap05 gap this wave's instructions target does not apply here and no second proof template was added. Instead, following the fallback instruction, added a real subprocess dispatch shim mirroring mcpp-pack's src/mcpp_dispatch.rs.tmpl structure (read in full as the reference): cargo_cicd_dispatch.rs.tmpl generates src/cargo_cicd_dispatch.rs, one real std::process::Command-backed wrapper fn per live command (51 of 52 catalog rows -- the deprecated cc:doctor-bare row, cnv:verb "", is deliberately excluded via a second, independent `FILTER(?verb != "")` sparql: query, since `cargo-cicd doctor ""` is not a real invocation), invoking the real `cargo-cicd` binary directly (confirmed at ~/cargo-cicd/Cargo.toml's [[bin]] name = "cargo-cicd"; its own main.rs strip_cargo_subcommand_token only removes a leading "cicd" token when cargo itself injected one, so a direct `cargo-cicd <noun> <verb>` invocation reaches the identical clap parse `cargo cicd <noun> <verb>` would). cargo_cicd_dispatch_proof.rs.tmpl adds 9 real-behavior tests (Command::get_program/get_args introspection without spawning, plus two real ErrorKind::NotFound spawn-error tests guarded against a machine that happens to have cargo-cicd installed) -- mirroring mcpp_dispatch_proof.rs.tmpl's structure, with the per-wrapper existence/shape check driven by the same sparql: rows query as the dispatch shim itself (51 rows, not a hand-picked sample) so a dropped/renamed generated function fails to COMPILE, not merely fails an assertion. cargo_cicd_mod_wiring.rs.tmpl gained `pub mod cargo_cicd_dispatch;`. Live-verified end-to-end in a new committed consumer, examples/cargo-cicd-verify (real `ggen sync run` + `cargo test`, mirroring examples/praxis-core-verify's structure): 24/24 passing (15 catalog + 9 dispatch), a second sync byte-identical (idempotent), and drift-sensitivity proven via a real reversible ontology edit (renaming cc:git-status's cnv:verb from "status" to "statusdrift" and back) -- confirmed the generated wrapper fn renamed from git_status to git_statusdrift and back, AND surfaced a real, useful finding along the way: this pack's freeze_policy:checksum artifacts (all five: catalog, proof, reference doc, and now dispatch, dispatch-proof) do not silently auto-regenerate on ontology drift when the file is otherwise untouched -- ggen-engine's write.rs decision order means an unedited-but-now-stale file hits [FM-WRITE-005] 'exists with differing content; refusing silent clobber' rather than being rewritten, so picking up a real ontology change requires deleting the target file(s) (or a future `force: true` companion) before the next sync, not just running `ggen sync run` again; this is a fail-closed property already latent in every pre-Round-5 freeze_policy:checksum artifact this pack ships, not something Round 5 introduced. Still short of L3's 'common behaviors generated' bar: this is a *generic* dispatcher (shells out to the real binary) rather than a reimplementation of any command's actual behavior, so cargo-cicd's own logic still lives entirely in its own binary, not in ontology-specified logic -- matching mcpp-pack's own identically-scoped, already-disclosed limitation. Round 6 (2026-08-16, drift check) found two mismatches against ~/cargo-cicd's current on-disk state: (1) the Round 4 note above claimed the NounVerbError enum is #[non_exhaustive]; ~/clap-noun-verb/src/error.rs:10-11 is `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum NounVerbError {` with no #[non_exhaustive] anywhere in the file -- the 10 variant names themselves remain correct and verbatim, but the attribute claim did not match the source, and has been corrected above. (2) ~/cargo-cicd/src/nouns/ now contains 22 noun files, not 21: a new lsp.rs (added via commits 'feat(lsp): manufacture cargo-cicd-lsp workspace...' through 'fix(lsp): intercept lsp explain <CODE>...') defines a real #[verb("check")] command (`lsp check`) that postdates this pack's Round 5 (2026-07-21) audit and is not represented in ontology.ttl's 21-noun/52-row catalog (51 live + 1 deprecated cc:doctor-bare). This pack's "52 commands across 21 nouns" / "51 live rows" coverage claims are therefore no longer complete against the current target repo; the lsp noun is a known, disclosed gap not yet audited into the ontology.

for executable consumer bodies and construction-only helpers for execution policies. Generated
construction can be compiled by a consumer, but marketplace qualification does not actuate a model,
tool, optimizer, or Parallel workload.

Version 0.2 adds an optional Fortune-5 enterprise binding plane. It reuses the marketplace's existing
fortune5-architecture vocabulary by reference, keeps enterprise governance separate from portable
DSPy semantics, validates source/authority/promotion/rollback/receipt boundaries when a binding is

re-verify against a newer wasm4pm commit before trusting the edge list on a later pass. src/wasm4pm_crate_deps.rs.tmpl renders those edges into a real traversal module (depends_on lookup, transitive_dependencies DFS with cycle-guard) -- genuine control flow driven by ontology data, not just a projected const array. wasm4pm_crate_mod_wiring.rs.tmpl is an inject-mode template that wires both generated modules into the consumer's src/lib.rs at the `// GENERATED catalogs/emission surfaces` marker (the same marker convention examples/receiptctl already uses), so a consumer no longer hand-writes the `mod` declarations. packs.name: dspy-pack
packs.description:
Universal DSPy generation vocabulary, verified against the real installed dspy 3.1.3 source tree
(not docs prose) via inspect.signature() on every admitted constructor and compile() method, and
real object construction/execution against actual dspy classes. Pure law -- ontology.ttl ships
zero individuals, so composing this pack cannot inject any signature, module, or optimizer into a
consumer's generated src/dspy_program.py / src/dspy_optimize.py. A consumer project supplies its
own individuals against this vocabulary in its own .ttl.

dspy:Signature/InputField/OutputField -- typed fields admit a primitive dspy:pythonType
(str/int/float/bool), a Literal[...]/List[Literal[...]] enum (dspy:hasLiteralOption), int
ge/le bounds (dspy:geInt/leInt), or a generated pydantic.BaseModel type
(dspy:hasPydanticModelType) -- exactly one of the three per field.

dspy:Module -- 13 of dspy 3.1.3's real Module classes: Predict, ChainOfThought, ReAct (with
dspy:usesMCPServer -> dspy:MCPServerConnection for MCP tool discovery, per dspy.ai's "DSPy + MCP"
tutorial), ProgramOfThought, MultiChainComparison, RLM, CodeAct (with dspy:hasLocalTool
scaffolded stubs), BestOfN/Refine (which wrap another Module via dspy:wrapsModule instead of a
Signature), Pipeline (an ordered linear composition of steps with real data-flow ArgBindings --
the verified retrieve-then-reason/RAG pattern), MultiHop (a fixed, parameterized
query-gen/retrieve/accumulate-context/answer-gen recipe, also verified by real execution), and
KNN/Parallel (previously excluded -- see below).

dspy:Optimizer -- 16 of dspy 3.1.3's real Teleprompter subclasses: GEPA, GRPO, BootstrapFewShot,
BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch, BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna, BootstrapFinetune, COPRO,
SignatureOptimizer, MIPROv2, AvatarOptimizer, BetterTogether (wraps another Optimizer via
dspy:wrapsPromptOptimizer/wrapsWeightOptimizer), InferRules, SIMBA, LabeledFewShot, Ensemble
(previously excluded -- see below), KNNFewShot (previously excluded -- see below). Each
optimizer's real, per-kind constructor AND compile() parameter names are followed exactly --
these vary meaningfully (SignatureOptimizer's compile() takes devset= not trainset=; COPRO/
SignatureOptimizer require an eval_kwargs dict; BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna's compile() requires
max_demos). Three real UPSTREAM dspy 3.1.3 defects are documented as caveats directly on the
relevant ontology properties (not hidden): SignatureOptimizer is unexported and its deprecated
shim is broken; AvatarOptimizer calls a removed dspy.TypedPredictor; BetterTogether has a
narrower runtime optimizer whitelist than its type signature suggests.

2026-08-10: composition/retrieval/KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot support added, closing every
gap the pack previously excluded. dspy.Retrieve, the retrieve-then-reason (RAG) pattern, the
2-hop query-gen/retrieve/accumulate/answer-gen loop, and dspy.KNN/dspy.Parallel/dspy.Ensemble/
dspy.KNNFewShot construction+execution were each actually built and run against the real
installed dspy 3.1.3 (not assumed from docs) -- see dspy:PipelineStep/dspy:ArgBinding,
dspy:EmbedderConfig, and the "MultiHop"/"Pipeline"/"KNN"/"Parallel"/"Ensemble"/"KNNFewShot"
dspy:kind values. dspy.Assert/dspy.Suggest were investigated and found fully removed from dspy
3.x -- dspy:Refine/dspy:BestOfN, already modeled, are confirmed dspy's complete modern
replacement; no new construct was needed for that axis.

Metric/reward/reduce function BODIES, tool bodies, and trainset/valset/devset/eval_kwargs
contents are deliberately out of ontology scope (arbitrary, consumer-owned inputs) -- ggen
scaffolds NotImplementedError stubs and named placeholders in src/dspy_program.py /
src/dspy_optimize.py.

Covers dspy.ai's own tutorials verbatim (fetched/verified 2026-08-10): general Predict/
ChainOfThought modeling, MCP tool use (https://dspy.ai/tutorials/mcp/), GEPA optimization
(https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_ai_program/), RL/GRPO optimization
(https://dspy.ai/tutorials/rl_ai_program/), two GEPA worked examples --
gepa_facilitysupportanalyzer (Literal/List[Literal] enum fields) and gepa_trusted_monitor (int
ge/le bounds) -- plus the retrieve-then-reason RAG pattern and 2-hop multi-hop pattern (both
directly executed against dspy.utils.dummies.DummyLM/dummy_rm this session). Fourteen real,
generated-and-tested example fixtures (ontology.ttl + ggen.toml, one per fixture family:
MCP/ReAct, GEPA Literal fields, all 9 original Module kinds, three optimizer families, Pydantic
model fields, Pipeline/RAG, MultiHop, KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot, plus a 4-fixture
"playground" set of dspy's most common tutorial-first patterns -- bare-Predict QA,
ChainOfThought math reasoning with a typed float output, Literal-constrained classification,
ChainOfThought summarization) live in the ggen monorepo's own examples/<name>/ directories and
are wired into that repo's `cargo test` suite (crates/ggen-engine/tests/dspy_pack_e2e.rs) --
each verified this pack version by running the real `ggen sync` pipeline and
constructing/executing the real generated dspy objects with zero exceptions
(Pipeline/MultiHop/KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot and all four playground fixtures
additionally verified by real Python execution against dspy 3.1.3, not just by inspecting the
rendered source text).

both graph engines (see crates/ggen-engine/tests/reasoner_independence_e2e.rs).

(evidence/checks.ttl) as an [ontology] source, and run the emitter before
sync (e.g. `just verify-tcps` = emitter -> sync -> receipt verify). The
freshness gate binds evidence to the latest ggenr:Sync receipt, so it
requires [law] reflexive = true in the consumer; staleness detection lags
one sync by construction (documented in gates/030_evidence_fresh.rq).

~/gymact/src/gymact/gyms/sregym.py::SREGYM_CAPABILITIES declares 14 real capabilities (all
Consequence.DO -- observe_cluster_state, run_kubectl, submit_diagnosis, submit_mitigation,

in the real gymact source -- only these 5 exist", which is now FALSE against the real,
currently-installed gymact source (confirmed directly, 2026-08-11): the real source has grown
to 14. This is not a hypothetical failure mode this pack guards against -- it is a real,
already-happened instance of exactly the drift this pack's gates exist to catch, found while
authoring this pack, not invented as a motivating example.

This pack does not fix that drift (fixing gymact_capabilities.toml to be GENERATED from this
pack's admitted facts is out of scope for this version -- named follow-up, lives in a
different repo). It provides the shared vocabulary (dcp:Capability / dcp:LabAllowlist /
dcp:CapabilitySourceManifest) and the two gates (exact-count-per-source,

a different, markdown-blob shape; this pack picks the richer, SPARQL-queryable

packs.name: pack-maturity-pack
packs.description:
Generates the cross-cutting proof artifacts that any ggen pack's own
consumer project can compose in to help close three of the twelve L5
promotion capabilities (l5p:cap03..l5p:cap12, http://ggen.org/l5-promotion#,
as defined in the ggen repository's own .specify/pack-l5-promotion.ttl):

- l5p:cap03 (Deterministic regeneration) and l5p:cap04 (Fixed-point
  convergence): a generated test that runs `ggen sync run` twice against
  the real consumer, snapshots every output file's SHA-256 before and
  after the second run, and asserts they are byte-identical -- a real
  filesystem observation, not trusting ggen's own "written"/"skipped"
  self-report (which is not itself a reliable idempotency signal: some
  frontmatter modes report "written" on every run even when content is
  unchanged, confirmed empirically against clap-noun-verb-zeroconfig-pack
  before this pack was built).
- l5p:cap09 (Generated receipts): a generated test that runs a real sync,
  then `ggen receipt verify`, and asserts the chain is valid, signed, and
  signature_valid.

Deliberately scoped to exactly these three -- no per-pack domain ontology
is required to compose this pack's tests (no `sparql:` extraction, plain
static-content templates), which is what makes them generic across ANY
consumer. This does NOT close l5p:cap01/02/05/06/07/08/10/11/12: those
require domain-specific ontology facts (what the subsystem actually does,
what a negative-witness mutation should look like, what provenance/release
surface the target needs) that only the consuming pack's own author can
supply -- a generic pack cannot manufacture domain semantics it doesn't
have. Composing this pack is a floor, not a ceiling: it gets a consumer
partway toward L4 on the maturity spine's "Regeneration lifecycle"
dimension (docs/packs/PACK_MATURITY_MODEL.md in the ggen repository),
never the whole bar by itself.

Verified 2026-08-10 against a real composed consumer (real ggen 26.8.6
binary, no mocks): both generated tests pass. A real negative-control
experiment was also run -- hand-editing a generated `force: true` file
between two real syncs -- and the mutation was silently overwritten by
the second sync (self-healing regeneration, the correct/intended
behavior for `force: true` templates), NOT flagged as a fixed-point
violation. This is disclosed precisely rather than rounded up to "catches
tampering": the regeneration test's real, verified purpose is catching
genuine non-determinism in the generation pipeline itself (a stray
timestamp, random ID, or unstable iteration order leaking into rendered
output), not external hand-edits to `force: true` output -- those are
expected to heal, by design, and this test correctly does not flag them.

packs.name: shacl-to-pydantic-pack
packs.description:
Second real projection target proving genuine reuse of packs/shacl-projection-pack's shared
SHACL-shape-driven-projection vocabulary (sp:derivedFromShape / sp:isPrimaryOutput), not a
parallel theory: projects a real sh:NodeShape into a real pydantic.BaseModel Python class.

sp:PydanticModel -- one individual per generated class (sp:className, dcterms:description
optional). sp:derivedFromShape ?shape (reused by IRI from shacl-projection-pack) supplies the
class's fields from ?shape's real sh:property list -- the exact same sh:path/sh:datatype
pattern packs/dspy-pack's dspy:Signature derivation and this pack's own pydantic derivation
both consume, so a single shape can, in principle, feed either target without rewriting the
shape.

templates/shacl_to_pydantic.py.tmpl's SPARQL/Tera echoes literals already computed by the
frontmatter SPARQL -- field name (from sh:path's local name), Python type (mapped from
sh:datatype, the same 4-type mapping shacl-projection-pack's gate admits), and description
(sh:description / dcterms:description, defaulted to the field name only when truly absent) --
never synthesizing new content, per pack-authoring-pack's "templates echo, they never
synthesize" rule.

Ships zero gates of its own. It relies entirely on packs/shacl-projection-pack's
gates/010_shape_validity.rq for shape-validity admission -- this is the real, confirmed
mechanism (see shacl-projection-pack's own pack.toml for the precise limitation: ggen packs
cannot declare pack-to-pack dependencies; a consumer must compose BOTH packs in its own
ggen.toml [packs] table for the shared gate to actually run). A consumer that composes only
this pack, without shacl-projection-pack, gets the template but no admission gate -- confirmed
by real `ggen sync run` in this pack version (see crates/ggen-engine/tests/
shacl_projection_pack_e2e.rs).

Ships zero individuals (pure law) -- composing this pack injects no pydantic model into a
consumer's generated src/. A consumer supplies its own sp:PydanticModel / sh:NodeShape
individuals in its own .ttl.
